rule_metadata.rule_name_english: Relational Categories of Letters: Mutamathilayn, Mutajanisayn, and Mutaqaribayn
rule_metadata.description: Comprehensive rules governing how identical, homogeneous, and close articulation letters interact when the first is vowelless (Saakin) and the second has a vowel (Mutaharrik).

theoretical_foundation.core_concept: When two letters meet—where the first is Saakin (vowelless) and the second is Mutaharrik (vowelled)—their relationship falls into one of three categories based on their Makhraj (articulation point) and Sifaat (attributes).

categories.definition: Two letters that share the exact same name, Makhraj, and Sifaat (e.g., Baa meeting Baa, Dal meeting Dal).

sub_divisions.saghir: Mutamathilayn Saghir: First letter is Saakin, second is Mutaharrik. **Rule: Mandatory Idgham (Merging)** in almost all cases.
sub_divisions.kabeer: Mutamathilayn Kabeer: Both letters are Mutaharrik. **Rule: Izhar (Clear)** for Hafs, except in specific words like مَأْمُنِيْ.
sub_divisions.mutlaq: Mutamathilayn Mutlaq: First letter is Mutaharrik, second is Saakin. **Rule: Izhar (Clear)**.

example.transliteration: Idh thahaba -> Izh-thahaba (Wait: Thal meeting Thal -> Idh-thahaba or Idh-thal)
example.breakdown: Dal meeting Dal. The first vowelless Dal merges completely into the second Dal: Qad-dakhalu -> Qad-dakhalu with Tashdeed.

categories.definition: Two letters that share the **exact same Makhraj (articulation point)** but **differ in some Sifaat (attributes)**.

key_groups_in_hafs.description: They share the tip of the tongue and upper gum line. When Saakin meets Mutaharrik among these three, Idgham occurs.

examples.breakdown: Ta meeting Dal -> Ta merges into Dal.

examples.note: Exception where Idgham is incomplete due to Istila of Taa.

key_groups_in_hafs.description: Tip of tongue and upper teeth edges.

example.transliteration: Yarkab-ma'ana (In Surah Hud, Hafs recites this with complete Idgham of Ba into Meem: Yarkam-ma'ana).

categories.definition: Two letters whose **Makharij are very close to each other** or **whose Sifaat are closely linked**.

key_instances.pair: Noon Sakinah meeting La, Ra, Ya, Waw, Meem (Yarmaloon)
key_instances.description: Technically classified under Mutaqaribayn or Mutajanisayn depending on the exact letter.
In the verse: أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ (Surah Al-Mursalat), the Qaf meets Kaf. Hafs allows complete or incomplete Idgham (Idgham Kaamil or Naqis).

practical_examples.breakdown: Identical Dal letters meeting; the first is vowelless, so it merges completely into the second with Tashdeed.
Ta and Dal share the same articulation point. Vowelless Ta merges into Dal.
Qaf merges into Kaf due to proximity of articulation.

assessment_bank.question: What does 'Al-Mutamathilayn' mean in Tajweed?
options: Two letters with completely different exit points

assessment_bank.question: What is the rule for Mutamathilayn Saghir (first letter Saakin, second Mutaharrik)?
What defines 'Al-Mutajanisayn' (Homogeneous letters)?
options: Letters that share the exact same Makhraj (articulation point) but differ in some attributes
Letters found only at the start of surahs

assessment_bank.question: What defines 'Al-Mutaqaribayn'?
options: Letters whose Makharij or Sifaat are close to each other

assessment_bank.question: In the phrase 'قَدْ دَخَلُوا', what relationship exists between the two Dals?
How is 'قَدْ دَخَلُوا' recited according to Tajweed rules?
options: With clear separation of both Dals

assessment_bank.question: In 'أَجَابَتْ دَعْوَتُكُمَا', which two letters interact under Mutajanisayn?
In 'إِذْ ظَلَمُوا', how does Thal interact with Zhhaa?
In Surah Hud, how does Hafs recite 'يَرْكَبْ مَعَنَا' regarding Ba and Meem?
options: Complete Idgham of Ba into Meem (Yarkamma'ana)

assessment_bank.question: In 'أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ', what relationship exists between Qaf and Kaf?
What is 'Mutamathilayn Kabeer'?
options: When both meeting letters carry vowels (Mutaharrik)
When the first letter is Saakin
When letters are in different words

assessment_bank.question: What is the general rule for Mutamathilayn Kabeer for Hafs?
What is 'Mutamathilayn Mutlaq'?
options: First letter Mutaharrik, second letter Saakin

assessment_bank.question: What is the rule for Mutamathilayn Mutlaq?
Why do Ta, Dal, and Taa form a Mutajanisayn group?
options: Because they share the tip of the tongue and upper gum line

assessment_bank.question: If a reciter fails to merge the vowelless Dal into the vowelled Dal in 'قَدْ دَخَلُوا', what kind of error is committed?
In 'بْتُّ', as in 'قَالَتْ طَائِفَةٌ' or similar, how do Taa and Ta interact?
What distinguishes Mutajanisayn from Mutamathilayn?
options: Mutamathilayn letters are 100% identical; Mutajanisayn letters share an exit point but have different attributes

assessment_bank.question: What distinguishes Mutaqaribayn from Mutajanisayn?
options: Mutaqaribayn letters have close (not identical) exit points or attributes

assessment_bank.question: In 'فَلْتَسْتَجِبُوا' or similar contexts, how are letters grouped?
Is Idgham mandatory for all Mutamathilayn Saghir instances?
options: Yes, with very few exceptions (like Ha' as-Sakt in Haqgalah)

assessment_bank.question: What happens in 'مَالِيَهْ ۜ هَلَكَعَنِّي' (Ha' as-Sakt exception)?
options: The two identical Ha' letters are read with Izhar (or Sakt) instead of Idgham because of the pause sign

assessment_bank.question: In 'رَبِحَتْ تِجَارُهُمْ', what interaction occurs between Taa and Ta?
In 'فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارُهُمْ', how should it be pronounced?
Which category covers the interaction between Lam and Ra in certain contexts?
Why is understanding Mutamathil, Mutajanis, and Mutaqarib essential for an advanced Tajweed app?
options: Because advanced Quranic recitation rules require handling letter assimilation beyond just Noon Sakinah
Because it is required for spelling
Because it is only for children

assessment_bank.question: In 'أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ', what are the two possible valid recitations for Hafs regarding Qaf and Kaf?
What is 'Saghir' (Small) classification in these three categories?
options: First letter is Saakin (vowelless) and second is Mutaharrik (vowelled)
Letters are written in small font
Letters occur at the end of Ayahs

assessment_bank.question: What is 'Kabeer' (Big) classification?
What is 'Mutlaq' classification?
options: First letter has a vowel, second letter is vowelless

assessment_bank.question: In 'بْل قُلْ' or similar, how do Lam and Lam interact?
In 'كْتُبْ', if it met another letter, how would it be classified?
Does Mutajanisayn Idgham apply to 'ذ' and 'ظ' in all recitations?
options: Yes, specifically in 'إِذْ ظَلَمُوا' for Hafs 'an 'Asim

assessment_bank.question: What is the physical sensation of pronouncing Mutamathilayn Saghir with Idgham?
options: The articulators strike once with double force and duration (Shaddah) without stopping
The breath is held in the throat

assessment_bank.question: In 'يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ', what letter interaction takes place?
Why are letters like Ba and Meem considered Mutajanisayn in specific phrases like 'يَرْكَبْ مَعَنَا'?
options: Because they both originate from the lips (Ash-Shafatan)

assessment_bank.question: How should your app's AI audio analyzer score a student who fails to merge Mutamathilayn Saghir letters?
options: Flag as a rule assimilation error (missing Idgham)

assessment_bank.question: In 'وَقُلْ رَبِّ', how do Lam and Ra interact?
What is the ultimate educational goal of teaching these three categories in your app?
options: To transition students from basic Noon rules to mastering absolute fluency and professional recitation mechanics across the entire Quran

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the core rule governing Mutamathil, Mutajanis, and Mutaqarib in Saghir form:
options: When vowelless letters meet identical, homogeneous, or close letters, Idgham (assimilation) takes place with specific exceptions
